land.text: the Transcaucasian federation of 22 April-26 May 1918, from which Georgia seceded

predecessors.note: The DRG page: 'On 22 April 1918, the Sejm ... declared the Transcaucasus an independent' state; 'the federation collapsed on 26 May 1918, when Georgia declared independence.' No dossier exists for the federation (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

The 1991 rebirth: 'Independence from the Soviet Union, declared 9 April 1991, finalized 26 December 1991' (Georgia page). The Georgian SSR dossier names this slug as its predecessor (1921) and successor (1992).

land.text: the whole of the Democratic Republic, occupied by the Red Army in February-March 1921

successors.note: The state is interrupted, not ended: the Georgian SSR (1921-1991) holds the land until the republic returns in 1991 (ledger loss 1921, gain 1991). identity.end is 2024 because the state is alive today.

capitals.name: Tiflis (Tbilisi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Tiflis (present-day Tbilisi)'. The government went into exile on 18 March 1921, to France.

correction.text: not Georgia: Iberia (Kartli) under its presiding princes, drawn as principality-of-iberia (its _588 keyframe, 588-681)

The Kingdom of Iberia page: 'The Arabs reached Iberia around 645 and compelled its eristavi (prince)'; the principality that follows the kingdom is drawn in principality-of-iberia, whose new keyframe principality-of-iberia_588 covers 588-681 with the region Kartli. Not used for Georgia.

The page's 'Georgia regained control over Artvin, Ardahan, part of Batum province, Akhaltsikhe and Akhalkalaki' is undated and Cliopatria's shapes hold at most 3 of the 52 Artvin and Ardahan cells (1919), so those are not drawn (see notes). region.text: Georgia within the Cliopatria 1918 outline (the DRG infobox gives 75,110 km2 for 1918)

ledger.note: 1918, 26 May: Georgia declares independence at Tiflis. 'Independence declared: 26 May 1918'; 'the federation collapsed on 26 May 1918, when Georgia declared independence' (the Transcaucasian federation had been declared on 22 April 1918). The Act of Independence of Georgia is dated the same day.

region.text: Lori (Borchalo), 'detached from the Erivan guberniia in 1862 and added to the Tiflis guberniia'

ledger.note: 1918, 7 December: the Georgian-Armenian War begins over Lori. 'The border dispute turned into an open military conflict on 7 December 1918'; Armenian forces captured Vorontsovka, Sanahin and Alaverdi by 15 December and advanced into Georgia proper on 16 December, taking Bolnis-Khachen on 18 and Shulaver on 20 December; the Georgians broke through on 28 December.

1919: Georgia takes over the Ottoman-held south (Akhaltsikhe, Akhalkalaki). The DRG page says only 'Georgia regained control over Artvin, Ardahan, part of Batum province, Akhaltsikhe and Akhalkalaki' (Borders), with no date; 1919 is where Cliopatria's shape grows (+7 cells of Samtskhe-Javakheti, +4 more in 1920). Artvin and Ardahan are not drawn (Cliopatria holds at most 3 of their 52 cells, in 1919, and the page gives no date).

1919, January: the Georgian-Armenian War ends. 'Battles continued until the ceasefire came into effect at midnight on December 31' and 'The Allied, Georgian and Armenian officials met to discuss a final settlement from 9 to 17 January 1919'; the DRG page has the Lori 'neutral zone' created under British intervention (undated).

region.text: Batum (Batumi) and Adjara, 'British-held Batumi remained out of Georgia's control until 1920'

ledger.note: 1920: Batum is incorporated. 'Batum was finally incorporated into the republic after the British evacuated the area in 1920'; 'British-held Batumi remained out of Georgia's control until 1920'. The page gives no day.

1920, end of the year: Georgia reoccupies the Lori neutral zone. The Lori 'neutral zone' was 'later reoccupied by Georgia after the fall of the Armenian Republic at the end of 1920' (Borders); the page gives no exact date, so the month is the end of the year. Cliopatria's 1920 shape holds only 2 of Lori's 15 cells.

region.text: the whole republic as the Red Army entered it from Azerbaijan and Armenia

ledger.note: 1921, 11/12 February: the Red Army invades. 'The Soviet invasion of Georgia (12 February - 17 March 1921)'; the night attacks that began it were on 11-12 February; the DRG infobox gives 'Soviet invasion: 11 February-17 March 1921'.

1921, 17 March: the invasion ends. 'Soviet invasion: 11 February-17 March 1921' (DRG infobox); Tbilisi fell on 25 February ('On 25 February, the triumphant Red Army entered Tbilisi'), Batumi was held until the battle of 18-19 March, and the Menshevik government sailed into exile (18 March).

region.text: the whole Democratic Republic of Georgia as Cliopatria draws it for 1920-1921

ledger.note: 1921, March: the Democratic Republic ends and its land becomes the Georgian SSR. 'On 25 February, the triumphant Red Army entered Tbilisi'; invasion ended 17 March, government in exile 18 March; the Georgian SSR dossier gains 'the rest of Georgia' in March 1921. The DRG page: 'Artvin, Ardahan and part of Batumi provinces were ceded to Turkey, Armenia gained control of Lori, and Azerbaijan obtained the Zaqatala district' (undated, in the treaties of March and October 1921); none of those is drawn here since Cliopatria's shape holds (at most 3 cells of) Artvin and Ardahan and none of Zaqatala. The Soviet annexation is dated 30 December 1922 in the infobox.

region.text: the Tskhinvali area of the former South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast

ledger.note: 1991: war over South Ossetia. After the Georgian Supreme Council 'passed a bill' on 11 December 1990 abolishing the oblast's autonomy and South Ossetia's sovereignty declaration of 20 September 1990, 'war broke out when Georgian police forces and paramilitary organizations entered the capital' (Tskhinvali); the page gives no date, only 'the 1991-1992 war'.

minus.text: the former South Ossetian Autonomous Oblast around Tskhinvali

region.text: the Georgian SSR's land: Cliopatria's 1992 outline (68,876 km2; infobox 69,700 km2 for the whole country), the South Ossetian oblast excepted

ledger.note: 1991, 9 April: Georgia declares independence from the Soviet Union (finalized 26 December 1991). 'On 9 April 1991, shortly before the collapse of the Soviet Union' the Supreme Council declared independence; infobox 'Declared 9 April 1991, Finalized 26 December 1991'. The land is Cliopatria's 1992 outline without the Tskhinvali area (separately held by the South Ossetians from 1990 in the republic-of-south-ossetia dossier).

region.text: the Tskhinvali, Java and Znauri districts

ledger.note: 1992, 24 June: the Sochi Agreement ends the South Ossetian war. 'A ceasefire agreement (the Sochi Agreement) was reached on 24 June 1992'; a Russian, Georgian and Ossetian peacekeeping force was set up. 'The separatists retained control over the districts of Tskhinvali, Java, Znauri and parts of Akhalgori'; Tbilisi kept the rest of Akhalgori and the Georgian villages in the Tskhinvali district.

1992, 14 August: Georgian forces enter Abkhazia and the war begins. 'On August 14, the National Guard of Georgia entered Abkhazia.' The Abkhaz Supreme Soviet's move of 23 July 1992 'must be construed as a declaration of independence'; the Abkhaz took Gagra on 2 October.

1993, 27 September: Sukhumi falls and the war ends. 'After a fierce battle, Sukhumi fell on 27 September'; infobox 'Result: Abkhazia becomes a de facto independent republic', period '14 August 1992 - 30 September 1993'. A Russian-brokered ceasefire had been signed on 27 July 1993 (Sochi agreement). The republic-of-abkhazia dossier ends its contest in 1994.

region.text: Abkhazia without the Upper Kodori Valley

ledger.note: 1993, 27 September: Abkhazia passes to the Abkhaz. 'Soon Abkhaz forces and the Confederates overran the whole territory of Abkhazia', but 'the upper Kodori Valley remained in Georgian hands' (the Fall of Sukhumi section).

region.text: the Georgian towns the Russian army held outside Abkhazia and South Ossetia in August 2008

ledger.note: 2008, August: Russian forces occupy Georgian towns beyond the conflict zones. 'Russian forces advanced into western Georgia from Abkhazia on 11 August' (Zugdidi, Senaki, where they took a military base) and held Gori until 22 August ('The occupation lasted until 22 August'); Poti was attacked from the air on 8 August. The disks (Gori 25 km, Zugdidi 30 km, Senaki 25 km) are my reading of the towns, which the gazetteer lacks.

intersect.text: the Upper Kodori Valley, the only part of Abkhazia Georgia still held

ledger.note: 2008, August: the Upper Kodori Gorge falls to the Abkhaz. 'Three days later [after 9 August], a military offensive against the Kodori Gorge was officially initiated by Abkhaz separatists'; the page gives no day (about 12 August). Russia recognised Abkhazia on 26 August 2008.

region.text: the Akhalgori district (Georgian-held until August 2008) and the Georgian villages near Tskhinvali

ledger.note: 2008, August: South Ossetians take Akhalgori. 'South Ossetian forces occupied Akhalgori' (a paragraph dated 17 August; no exact day); the Georgian-held villages of the Tskhinvali district were also lost. Russia recognised South Ossetia on 26 August 2008.

region.text: the Georgian towns the Russian army held outside Abkhazia and South Ossetia

ledger.note: 2008, 8 October: Russian forces leave the buffer areas. 'Russian forces pulled back from the buffer areas bordering Abkhazia and South Ossetia on 8 October 2008'; troops had begun withdrawing from western Georgia on 13 September. Perevi was held until 18 October 2010.

wars.name: Georgian-Armenian War
wars.outcome: Ceasefire at midnight on 31 December 1918 after British and French intervention; a neutral zone follows, the final settlement left to the Paris Peace Conference.
wars.note: 7-31 December 1918; Georgia reoccupies the zone after the fall of the Armenian Republic at the end of 1920 (DRG page).

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: Soviet victory: Tbilisi falls on 25 February, the government leaves on 18 March; Turkey claims Ardahan and Artvin (ultimatum of 23 February) and drops its claim to Batumi (Treaty of Kars, 13 October 1921).

wars.name: Georgian-Ossetian conflict (South Ossetia War, 1991-1992)

zones.text: the Tskhinvali, Java and Znauri districts

wars.outcome: Sochi ceasefire of 24 June 1992; separatists keep Tskhinvali, Java, Znauri and parts of Akhalgori; Georgia keeps the Georgian villages and the rest of Akhalgori.
wars.note: The page gives no start date for the fighting.

wars.name: Georgian Civil War (1991-1993)
wars.outcome: Zviad Gamsakhurdia, elected president on 26 May 1991, was 'soon deposed in a bloody coup d'etat, from 22 December 1991 to 6 January 1992'; 'a bitter civil war ... lasted until December 1993'. No border moved.
wars.note: 'Zviadists' stands for the supporters of Gamsakhurdia; no dossier is asked.

wars.name: War in Abkhazia (1992-1993)
wars.outcome: Abkhaz victory: Sukhumi falls on 27 September 1993; 'Abkhazia becomes a de facto independent republic'; Georgia keeps the Upper Kodori Valley.
wars.note: Ceasefires of 3 September 1992 and 27 July 1993 failed; Gagra fell on 2 October 1992.

wars.name: Russo-Georgian War
wars.outcome: Russian victory: ceasefire negotiated by Sarkozy on 12 August; Russia recognises Abkhazia and South Ossetia on 26 August; Georgia loses Akhalgori and the Upper Kodori Gorge; Russian forces leave the buffer areas on 8 October 2008.

certainty.note: The republic's frontiers were disputed with Armenia (Lori, the neutral zone), Azerbaijan (Zaqatala), Turkey (Artvin, Ardahan, Batum) and the Volunteer Army (Sochi), and 'border disputes' fill the DRG page's Borders section; Cliopatria's outline is approximate.
The state is absent (the Georgian SSR dossier draws the land); the era is covered only so the certainty list has no gap.

International frontiers of a UN member state, drawn along the former Georgian SSR line (no page opened dates a delimitation, so this is the researcher's judgment). The ceasefire lines with Abkhazia and South Ossetia are sharp but not recognised.

notes:
THE ROW IS SPLIT. Cliopatria's Georgia (567..2024, 17 shapes) is four states: georgia_567 (567-576) is Lazica (reviewed in the lazica dossier, which lists the Name); georgia_638 (638-646) is Iberia/Kartli (verdict wrong here; it belongs to principality-of-iberia, whose _588 keyframe covers 588-681); georgia_724..980 (the Abkhazian kingdom, 724-1009) are reviewed in kingdom-of-abkhazia (eu-19-x, cliopatria_names ["Georgia"]); this dossier is modern Georgia (1918-1921 and 1991-2024). The validator therefore warns about the 11 shapes it leaves to those dossiers: expected. No new slug: 'georgia' is kept for the state that the georgian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier already points at, as both predecessor and successor.

TWO LIVES, ONE STATE. The Democratic Republic of Georgia (26 May 1918-1921) and the Republic of Georgia (1991-) are one dossier here because the Georgian SSR dossier and the page ('continues to be an inspiration for contemporary Georgia') link them; the interruption is the ledger's loss in March 1921 and gain in April 1991 with counterpart georgian-soviet-socialist-republic, and identity.end is 2024 as for a living state. The orchestrator may prefer two dossiers (the Armenian and Azerbaijani republics are split that way in Cliopatria); in that case the 1921 loss becomes a dissolve and the 1991 gain a found.

CORRECTIONS TO CLIOPATRIA: (1) Adjara and Batum are removed from the 1918 and 1919 shapes (the page: incorporated in 1920); (2) the 1992-2023 shape is the de jure country, so South Ossetia (from 1990-92), Abkhazia (from September 1993, the Upper Kodori from August 2008) and Akhalgori (August 2008) are cut out to match the republic-of-abkhazia and republic-of-south-ossetia dossiers, whose ledgers record the same transfers as gains with counterpart georgia; (3) 1991 has no Cliopatria shape.

NOT DRAWN (undated by the pages opened): Artvin, Ardahan and part of Batum province 'regained' from the Ottomans and ceded to Turkey in 1921; the Zaqatala district (Azerbaijan claimed it; 'never led to hostilities'); Sochi district 'briefly controlled in 1918-1919' (two Sochi cells are in every Cliopatria shape); the Volunteer Army; Lori and Zaqatala lost in 1921; Adjara's autonomy crisis of 2004 (no territorial change); the Treaty of Moscow of 7 May 1920 (recognition only). The georgian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier has a confidence-1 gain of the Artvin Okrug from georgia; with Artvin not drawn here, that event has no mirror (see its note).

DISAGREEMENTS: the Abkhaz war ends 27 September 1993 (Fall of Sukhumi; infobox 30 September) here, 1994 in republic-of-abkhazia; the South Ossetian war start is January 1991 in republic-of-south-ossetia but undated on the Georgian-Ossetian conflict page, so the contest here carries a year only; Georgia page area 69,700 km2 (infobox) vs 67,900 km2 (Geography section) vs Cliopatria 68,876 km2.

PAGE BUDGET: 8 pages against up to 9. Failed: South_Ossetia_War_(1991-1992) (url_not_found; Georgian-Ossetian conflict used instead). The Treaty of Kars and Batum pages, the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic page, the Zaqatala and Sochi disputes and the Adjara crisis were not opened.

GAZETTEER: Gori, Zugdidi, Senaki are not places in places.jsonl (lon/lat disks used); 'Mughan plain' is needed by balasagan.
